title: Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_M on gfx1151: a prefix-cache hit costs 24.9x the prefill per token of a miss and forfeits MTP entirely, so hits have no MTP path to open yet
purpose: Measure the prefix-cache hit rate on a realistic multi-turn load, and the hit path's own cost, to decide whether a prefix hit should be given a path into MTP instead of declining to autoregressive decode.
hardware: zbook, Ryzen AI MAX+ PRO 395 / Radeon 8060S (gfx1151)

server.command: python -m hipengine.server --model Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf --backend hip_gfx1151 --served-model-name qwen3.8-27b-q4km --max-context-tokens 8192 --kv-storage bf16 --execution-profile production --speculative-mtp-serving auto --speculative-candidate-budget 3 --prefix-cache {off,radix} --metrics prometheus --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8091 --log-level info

workload.note: Multi-turn mode: each dataset conversation becomes four growing prompts, so turn t submits the first t user turns and their dataset replies and every turn after the first shares a token-exact prefix with the turn before it. Prompts come from the dataset rather than from the model's own replies so both arms submit byte-identical prompt sequences. --route-mix assigns the arm per conversation, so one server process and one load carry the true-AR control and the MTP arm.

cost_of_a_hit.miss_outlier: the 12.6 ms/token miss row is the first measured request after server start (lazy graph capture); the other three misses are 2.8-3.4 ms/token
cost_of_a_hit.source_of_numbers: the backend's own per-request prefill_ms in the terminal chunk's timing block, divided by the prefix block's executed_prefill_tokens

mechanism.suffix_prefill_runs_at_decode_speed: hipengine/generation/qwen35_gguf.py: _prefill_native_chunk and _prefill_processed_argmax_chunk both take the `if row.prefix_reused_tokens:` branch and process the suffix with one `session.step(token_id)` per token, where the miss path calls the batched prefill. A single-token step costs the same as a decode step (82 ms at ~700 tokens of context), so the reuse path trades a 3.2 ms/token batched prefill for an 82 ms/token decode-shaped loop.
mechanism.mtp_declines_at_the_prompt_sink: hipengine/generation/qwen35_gguf_mtp2.py: _open_prompt_streaming_sinks returns None as soon as any row has prefix_reused_tokens > 0 (mtp2_prompt_fallback_reason = 'prefix_reuse_k0'). The provider therefore never receives the prompt's hidden rows, capability() reports no draft state, and every decode cycle reports no_provider: one event per output token, zero draft cycles.
mechanism.why_the_reused_prefix_cannot_supply_hidd: the draft provider is a stateful recurrent head whose catch-up replays the whole prompt position by position from the target's hidden rows (one row per prompt token). A reused prefix never ran the target in this request, so those rows do not exist; _catch_up_provider raises 'GGUF MTP2 prompt hidden rows do not align' if the array is short.
mechanism.the_retained_11_8x_measurement_is_a_one_: docs/CONCURRENCY.md's 249.269 -> 21.188 ms prefix slice is a p256+s1 packet: a one-token suffix makes the per-token loop cost exactly one step, which is the single shape where this implementation's weakness cannot show.

decision.mtp_row_for_hits: not opened: a hit already costs 24.9x the prefill per token and forfeits MTP, so admitting MTP on a hit would optimize the smaller half of a path that is 13x slower end to end than not using the cache at all
decision.prerequisite: batch the reused-prefix suffix through the same prefill entry the miss path uses, so a hit's suffix costs prefill speed instead of decode speed
decision.then: the draft checkpoint is the right mechanism for MTP on a hit: capture the provider's recurrent state at each 256-aligned boundary during the catch-up it already performs, and a later request matching that boundary restores it instead of replaying the prompt. Rebuilding the target's hidden rows for a reused prefix (the alternative) re-runs the target over the whole reused prefix, which is the cost reuse exists to remove
decision.measured_bound: even a perfect MTP-on-hit would not have rescued this load: decode is 10.4-10.6 s of a 31-70 s request on the hit rows, so the prefill fix is worth ~4x more than the decode fix

source.harness_changes: scripts/sharegpt_mtp_routing_pass.py: --turns N multi-turn expansion, per-row prefix telemetry from the terminal chunk's diagnostics, per-row backend timing, by_prefix and by_turn summary slices
